title: Set-Returning Functions & TABLE Output
description: Build table functions using RETURNS TABLE and generate series using generate_series().

data.text: A **Set-Returning Function (SRF)** returns a set of rows (a virtual table) rather than a single scalar value. SRFs can be called directly inside the `FROM` clause of queries.

data.title: Custom Set-Returning Table Function
data.content: Returning tabular records using RETURNS TABLE and RETURN QUERY.
data.code:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION get_active_subscribers_by_domain(p_domain TEXT)
RETURNS TABLE (
    subscriber_id INT,
    email VARCHAR,
    subscribed_at TIMESTAMPTZ
) AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT id, s.email, s.created_at
    FROM subscribers s
    WHERE s.email LIKE '%@' || p_domain
      AND s.is_active = true;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql STABLE;

data.text: `RETURNS TABLE (...)` is shorthand for a function with `OUT` parameters that returns a set. It is the cleanest way to expose a tabular result, and callers can treat it like a table in `FROM` or join it with `LATERAL`. `generate_series` is the built-in set-returning function you will use most often for date and number spines.

data.title: A reusable date spine function
data.content: The function returns one row per day in the range; a LATERAL join attaches daily totals and fills gaps with zero.
data.code:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION date_range(
    p_from date,
    p_to   date
)
RETURNS TABLE (d date)
LANGUAGE sql
STABLE
AS $$
    SELECT generate_series(p_from, p_to, interval '1 day')::date;
$$;

SELECT
    r.d,
    COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) AS revenue
FROM date_range('2024-01-01', '2024-01-31') AS r
LEFT JOIN orders AS o
    ON o.ordered_at::date = r.d
GROUP BY r.d
ORDER BY r.d;

data.title: Mark the volatility correctly
data.text: A function whose output depends only on its arguments is `IMMUTABLE`; one that reads tables or uses functions such as `now()` is `STABLE` (within a statement) or `VOLATILE`. Plain SQL functions that read the database should be `STABLE`, which lets the planner inline them while still re-reading data when needed. Mislabeling a table-reading function as `IMMUTABLE` can produce stale index contents.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Set-returning functions return tables via `RETURNS TABLE (...)`.
Use `RETURN QUERY` to stream rows directly from internal queries.
Call set-returning functions in the `FROM` clause like ordinary tables.
